articles.headline: Ruben Amorim uninterested in contributing to Man United discourse: 'Nothing to say'
articles.description: Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ルベン・アモリム、マンUに関する議論への関与を否定：「言うことは何もない」
articles.descriptionJa: ルベン・アモリムは、木曜夜にボーンマスで行われるACミランとのヨーロッパリーグの対戦を前に、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドについては「言うことは何もない」と強調した。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 14 months in charge, and was appointed by the Serie A side in June.

Amorim revealed he does not think he has changed as a person since his time with the Red Devils, but believes he has become better at his job.

"Overall, I think the important thing is that I'm here as AC Milan's manager," said Amorim, speaking at a press conference at the Vitality Stadium and quoted by Milan News.

"I have nothing to say about United. I can say that I loved the club and the atmosphere: what happened doesn't change that.

"Then I moved on, now I'm at AC Milan and I'm focused on this: at every big club, problems are always around the corner. I focus on ourselves and I don't think about the teams. My past at United doesn't matter; what I said when I signed there remains the same."

Amorim revealed Samuel Chukwueze is out with a hip problem, and Gonçalo Ramos has sustained a calf strain, and expects 19-year-old Alphadjo Cissè, who he believes has reached only "50 per cent of his potential" to feature in Thursday's line-up to face the Cherries.

"I have more experience as a coach, but I'm not a different person," Amorim added, reflecting on his spell with United.

"I understand football better, and that will help me deal with problems in the future. I think I'm the same person, just a little more experienced in some things."

The man who replaced Amorim at United, Michael Carrick, has seen his position come under serious pressure in recent weeks as the club have endured a torrid start to the new season. 

His team were beaten 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' Como in Italy on Wednesday in a match that saw Carrick and Fernandes appear to trade barbs through their post-match comments to the travelling media.

articles.headline: Panthers LB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) set to miss Week 7 game vs. Bucs
articles.description: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is preparing to host the Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズのLBジェイラン・フィリップス（ハムストリング）が第7週のバックス戦を欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: パンサーズのデイブ・カナレス監督は、日曜日に開催されるバッカニアーズ戦について、主力のアウトサイドラインバッカーであるジェイラン・フィリップスを欠いた状態で準備を進めていると述べた。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that the team is preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips.

Canales didn't offer a timeline for Phillips (hamstring) to return, but he avoided any gamesmanship on Phillips' status for Week 7.

When asked if the expectation was that Phillips would miss this week, with a "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Green Bay Packers on deck for Week 8, Canales noted that Phillips, who reinjured his left hamstring in the road win over the Philadelphia Eagles, needed to be treated with caution.

"I think I can fairly say that," Canales said about Phillips missing Week 7. "I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of."

Phillips left Sunday's win in the first half but returned late in the third quarter. On Wednesday, Phillips walked around the perimeter of the Panthers' practice field while his teammates participated in a walkthrough.

"Jaelan got that same hamstring [injury] -- we've got to take care of that now," Canales said. "So, we're going to still push it and evaluate him, but this is something we're going to have to be smart with. Two weeks off of the first injury and then he was able to finish the game, which was incredible for him to go back out there and do his job. But the MRIs, the findings, this is something that we're going to have to treat more intensively."

Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million deal in March, has produced 2.5 sacks on the season. The former Miami Dolphins and Eagles pass rusher was brought in, along with inside linebacker Devin Lloyd, to turn around a middling Carolina defense.

But this Sunday, like Lloyd in Week 3's loss to the Cleveland Browns, Phillips will need to watch from the sideline as he recovers from injury.

Canales declined to speculate whether Phillips would be able to play at Green Bay next week. For now, though, with Phillips and special teams ace Thomas Incoom (calf) sidelined, the Panthers plan to call up practice squad linebacker Nick Hampton. The former Los Angeles Rams pass rusher is known for his special teams ability, and he recently returned to the Panthers after being cut with an undisclosed injury during training camp

"It's the reason why we brought him back, and he was having a great camp before he had the injury," Canales said. "So, we're excited to see Nick this week, and then some of the other guys that we've been working with, they've got to be ready if we go that direction with more guys."

Incoom, according to Canales, is considered week-to-week and won't be immediately placed on injured reserve. Incoom was injured against the Eagles and Canales said it took four players to fill his role on special teams throughout the remainder of the Week 6 win.

articles.headline: Champions League recap: Como stun Man United, Bayern-Arsenal share points
articles.description: Como shocked Manchester United, while Bayern Munich and Arsenal played out to an entertaining 2-2 draw on a Wednesday full of UEFA Champions League action.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグまとめ：コモがマンUに番狂わせ、バイエルンとアーセナルは引き分け
articles.descriptionJa: UEFAチャンピオンズリーグの熱戦が繰り広げられた水曜日、コモがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに衝撃を与えた一方で、バイエルン・ミュンヘンとアーセナルは2-2の白熱した引き分けに終わった。
articles.body:
THE CHAMPIONS!

Another day meant another round of European heavyweights who were ready to battle it out on the biggest stage.

Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League continued Wednesday, with nine more matches across the continent and plenty of blockbuster clashes.

Among the standout fixtures, Arsenal traveled to Germany for a heavyweight showdown with Bayern Munich where both teams got a point as the game ended in a 2-2 draw, Real Madrid welcomed RB Leipzig to the Bernabéu and ended up winning 4-1, and Manchester United went to Italy to face Como in one of our two early matches, only for Michael Carrick's team to lose 4-1 in one of the worst losses in the club's history in the competition.

Elsewhere, Aston Villa took on Viking and won 3-1 and Internazionale bounced back from their defeat to Club Brugge as they defeated Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0.

Also on the schedule, we had Lille vs. Galatasaray in the other early match which saw the Turkish club win 4-2, Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0, Real Betis defeated Feyenoord 1-0 and LASK defeated Sporting CP 3-2.

Enjoy that happened from Wednesday's matches across Europe!

articles.headline: Diomande stunner caps Madrid win against former club Leipzig
articles.description: Real Madrid maintained their perfect start in the Champions League with an emphatic 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: ディオマンデの鮮烈なゴールで、レアルが古巣ライプツィヒに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは水曜日、RBライプツィヒに対して4-1の圧勝を収め、チャンピオンズリーグでの完璧なスタートを維持した。
articles.body:
Real Madrid maintained their perfect start in the Champions League with an emphatic 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

Bernardo Silva and Arda Güler struck either side of halftime at the Bernabeu before late goals from Kylian Mbappé and former Leipzig star Yan Diomande wrapped up a convincing win for the Spanish giants.

Leipzig were competitive for most of the first half but were outplayed after Silva's opener -- his first goal for Madrid -- after 43 minutes.

Güler poked in to double the lead and Mbappé could not be denied, claiming his 12th goal of the season after 83 minutes.

Tidiam Gomis did pull one back for the German side to make the score 3-1 but Diomande, who left Leipzig in a deal worth a potential €140 million ($189m) in the summer, had the final say with a stunning volley.

The game took some time to warm up with the first shot not arriving until Leipzig's Ridle Baku fired tamely at Thibaut Courtois after 20 minutes. Madrid countered immediately but Mbappé dragged an effort wide.

Leipzig threatened again when they broke from deep and David Raum's pass was deflected into the path of Rômulo but his shot was well saved by Courtois.

Vinícius Júnior tried his luck for Madrid after bursting down the left and cutting inside but Maarten Vandevoordt pushed his long-range attempt wide.

Antonio Nusa was lively for Leipzig on the left and had a shot blocked before delivering a cross for Romulo, but he could only head straight at Courtois.

Jude Bellingham blazed over for Madrid before Christopher Nkunku spurned a gilt-edged chance for Leipzig when he raced through on goal only to be denied by Courtois.

Madrid took control just before the interval when Silva pounced on a goalkeeping error.

Vandevoordt blocked Güler's initial strike with his foot but the ball squirmed between his legs and Silva snaffled the chance from close range.

Real chased more after the break with Federico Valverde bursting into the area and forcing a good save from Vandevoordt.

The hosts doubled their lead in the 52nd minute as Bellingham got to the byline and stood up a cross for Mbappe at the back post. The Frenchman rose and headed back across goal and Güler made sure it crossed the line.

Güler went close to another after exchanging passes with Valverde in a sweeping move but his first-time shot was too close to Vandevoordt.

Mbappé put the result beyond all doubt when he received a pass from Diomande on the edge of the area and curled a shot into the top corner.

Leipzig were not quite done and at least got on the scoresheet as Christoph Baumgartner cut through the defence to play in substitute Gomis for a consolation.

Madrid had the final word, however, as Diomande added their fourth with a thunderous volley from a Brahim Díaz cross.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Warriors exploring options to trade center Kristaps Porzingis
articles.description: The Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ウォリアーズがセンターのクリスタプス・ポルジンギスのトレード案を検討中
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズは、プライベートな健康問題で無期限欠場となっているベテランセンターのクリスタプス・ポルジンギスのトレードルートを模索し始めたと、リーグ関係者がESPNのシャムス・チャラニアに語りました。
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has him seriously contemplating his future in basketball, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December.

Despite the built-in flexibility, that wasn't the idealized intent of the contract. Porzingis played in 15 of the team's final 20 games last season and Warriors' management believed he had an encouraging enough summer to pencil Porzingis in as the projected starting center next to Draymond Green and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg in the frontcourt.

Porzingis was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the week leading up to training camp and attended Jimmy Butler's player-led event in San Diego in late September, though team sources described a detached Porzingis as indifferent and uninterested in participating in scrimmages and strenuous on-court prep work at the event.

On the Sunday before training camp, Porzingis called the Warriors and alerted general manager Mike Dunleavy that he was still dealing with the lingering impact of a health issue that has bothered him for nearly two years and told them he would be taking an indefinite leave of absence.

Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics, and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his energy level and ability to consistently play NBA basketball. Porzingis has termed it a POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) diagnosis, which can lead to bouts of dizziness, fatigue and brain fog.

After missing the first two weeks of training camp and the entire preseason, Porzingis drove up from Los Angeles to San Francisco last Tuesday, league sources said, to meet with Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini, the franchise's lead medical decision-maker.

In the aftermath, the team announced that they would keep the details of the meeting private, but expressed an expectation that Porzingis would remain around the team as he tried to improve his health and eventually resume his career.

But that hasn't been the case. Porzingis hasn't returned to the facility, league sources said, beginning another indefinite leave of absence where he is mostly maintaining contact with only Dunleavy and Celebrini. The Warriors listed him as out for the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night and the reasoning as "not with team" instead of an illness.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich snap Arsenal win streak in thrilling 2-2 draw
articles.description: Declan Rice stole the limelight from Harry Kane as Arsenal hit back to snatch a thrilling 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in a heavyweight clash Wednesday at the Allianz Arena.
articles.headlineJa: バイエルン、熱戦の2-2ドローでアーセナルの連勝を阻止
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日にアリアンツ・アリーナで行われた重量級の対決で、アーセナルが反撃を見せてバイエルン・ミュンヘンと2-2の劇的な引き分けに持ち込んだ。ハリー・ケインを抑え、デクラン・ライスが脚光を浴びた。
articles.body:
Declan Rice stole the limelight from Harry Kane as Arsenal hit back to snatch a thrilling 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in a heavyweight Champions League clash Wednesday at the Allianz Arena.

Gunners midfielder Rice lashed low beyond Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer eight minutes from time to extend his side's unbeaten start to this season's competition following back-to-back wins over Napoli and Lille.

The draw did, however, bring an end to Arsenal's 14-game winning streak in the UCL League Phase -- the second longest after Bayern in competition history.

Kane -- Tottenham's all-time record scorer -- was on course to claim the winner after registering his 16th goal in 23 career outings against Arsenal by converting a 61st-minute penalty following Jurrien Timber's handball.

The England captain, who is contention to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday, earlier produced a sublime assist for Alphonso Davies to cancel out Eberechi Eze's opener.

But in their biggest test since losing last season's final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties, Mikel Arteta's Premier League champions responded well to deservedly return home with a share of the spoils.

A pulsating draw in Bavaria was soured slightly by an early injury suffered by Bukayo Saka.

Noni Madueke was recalled in place of Eze following his late winner at Nottingham Forest on Sunday, with Timber coming in for Ben White in the Gunners' other change.

Meanwhile, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany was fit enough to take his place on the touchline after a viral infection.

Arsenal controlled the early exchanges before suffering a blow when Saka limped off to be replaced by Eze in the 10th minute.

With Michael Olise suspended, Jamal Musiala injured and Luis Díaz only on the bench, Bayern's attacking fear factor was significantly diminished.

Riccardo Calafiori threatened from a Martin Ødegaard corner before Arsenal were almost immediately caught out on the counterattack when a goal-kick taken by the quick-thinking Kane culminated in David Raya saving well from the unmarked Serge Gnabry.

Arsenal continued to dictate proceedings and edged ahead in the 25th minute. Eze was sent racing into Bayern's 18-yard box by Ødegaard's delightful ball over the top before rifling a left-footed shot beyond Neuer and into the bottom-right corner.

Celebrations were briefly halted by an offside flag, only for VAR to overturn the decision, to the delight of almost 3,800 travelling fans high up at the other end of the pitch.

However, Arsenal's lead lasted just 10 minutes.

Kane, who spent much of the game dropping deep, was the architect, producing a sumptuous through ball from inside the centre circle for Davies to outpace Timber and slot past Raya.

For all of their possession, Arsenal appeared vulnerable on transitions and could have gone into the break behind as Kane had an effort blocked before Gnabry picked the wrong option by shooting from distance.

articles.headline: Sources: Mavericks agree to two-way deal with Walter Clayton Jr.
articles.description: The Mavericks agree to a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：マーベリックス、ウォルター・クレイトン・Jr.と2ウェイ契約に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNの取材によると、マーベリックスは元ドラフト1巡目指名のウォルター・クレイトン・Jr.とNBAの2ウェイ契約を結ぶことで合意した。
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks have agreed on a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday.

Clayton was waived earlier this week by the Memphis Grizzlies ahead of the league's roster cut-down deadline. He is joining the Mavericks after clearing waivers.

Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr., Jock Landale, John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range.

Clayton, 23, was the No. 18 pick in the 2025 draft after helping Florida win its third national title. He was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player and was a consensus first-team All-American in 2025.

The Mavericks, still light on ball handlers despite the return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury, could use the depth Clayton provides in their backcourt.

Ross Barkley nodded Villa in front for his third goal in this season's competition already before Emi Buendia doubled their advantage from the spot and Henrik Heggheim's own goal made the result safe.

articles.headline: Ravens' Lamar Jackson returns to practice but status remains unclear vs. Bengals
articles.description: After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp.
articles.headlineJa: レイヴンズのラマー・ジャクソンが練習に復帰するも、ベンガルズ戦への出場は不透明
articles.descriptionJa: 練習後、ジャクソンは負傷した左足首をかばっており、チーム施設に入る際に明らかに足を引きずる様子が見られた。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson returned to practice Wednesday, but it remains uncertain whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp. He also walked with a limp inside the locker room.

Jackson wasn't present during the media availability portion of practice, but he later came out onto the practice field. This marked the first time that Jackson has had any on-field work since spraining his ankle 17 days ago.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter described Jackson as a limited participant, saying he "was able to get in a little bit of work and be involved in preparation." Minter also indicated Jackson participated in some team drills.

"There's nobody that wants to be out there more than Lamar," Minter said. "Lamar wants to play. But at the same time, you got to be healthy enough to play."

Jackson sprained his left ankle late in the first half of a 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. He had missed the past two games and the past six practices before returning Wednesday.

Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson, leading the Ravens to a comeback win at the Atlanta Falcons before struggling Sunday in a loss at the Cleveland Browns.

In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters without him, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns.

"He is working to get back," Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers said. "He is working every day, doing what he needs to do to get back on the field. That's all you can do when you're injured, just do everything you can to get back on the field." 

If Jackson can play Sunday, it would be a timely return. The Ravens (4-2) and the Bengals (3-2) are considered the top two teams in the AFC North.

Since Jackson became the starter midway through the 2018 season, the Ravens are 11-2 against the Bengals with Jackson, who has thrown 24 touchdowns and six interceptions against Cincinnati. Without Jackson over that span, Baltimore is 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals, losing by an average margin of 12 points.

"I know this, that when it's ready for him to be able to play and we feel like that's the best thing to do, that's what we'll do," Minter said.

articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 21: J.J. McCarthy named Giants' starting QB for Week 7

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The inevitable has finally arrived in New York: McCarthy is reportedly going to start at quarterback for the Giants in Week 7.

It was a decision destined to happen at some point following McCarthy's Sept. 28 acquisition from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick. And it was a decision almost assuredly destined to happen this week after the Michigan product delivered 16.52 fantasy points in the fourth quarter alone, nearly leading his Giants to a comeback from down 34-10 to the Saints.

McCarthy's installation doesn't promise any miracles, not for the Giants nor for fantasy, but it's an understandable, aggressive move that could positively shift the team's offensive dynamic.

First off, don't take McCarthy's Week 6 performance remotely to heart, as it's almost entirely meaningless for evaluative purposes. High-scoring relief efforts by quarterbacks aren't uncommon. Since 2021, there have been 13 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who made a start later in that season; that group averaged 5.2 fewer fantasy points as starters than in that relief appearance.

More relevant to McCarthy's cause is his extensive tape from his 10 mediocre (to say it gently) starts in Minnesota last season. In those starts, he was 28th in Total QBR (36.1), 30th in completion rate (57.6%), 28th in off-target rate (19.3%) and 30th in touchdown-to-interception ratio (0.9). He struggled mightily when throwing into crowded spaces, with the fourth-worst passer rating when targeting a receiver with three or fewer yards of separation, per Next Gen Stats.

What McCarthy did do that could have fantasy-relevance, however, was aim deep about as often as any quarterback in the league. His average depth of target of 8.8 yards led all quarterbacks who started at least half of their teams' games, though he did have seven interceptions on throws of at least 15 yards, putting his skill set into the extreme risk/reward category. Anyone who watched Sunday's game can attest to that, as McCarthy was chucking the ball in a desperate attempt to breathe some life into a Giants offense that, to that point, had shown barely any.

Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely each scored more than half of their Week 6 fantasy points after McCarthy entered the game, and the two combined for five catches on six targets for 130 yards and a touchdown on throws of at least 10 yards from McCarthy. articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 21

Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal

Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return.

Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season.

Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks

Sources: Warriors begin exploring trades for Porzingis

The Golden State Warriors have begun the process of looking for trades for center Kristaps Porzingis, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Porzingis remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has had him questioning his future with basketball.

If there isn't a breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from his career is possible, sources told Charania.

Join ESPN's Dave McMenamin for a Reddit AMA!

At 4 p.m. ET Wednesday, senior NBA writer Dave McMenamin will answer anything about the Los Angeles Lakers, the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James, the opening few days of the season and more!

Hoop Collective: Full reaction to the opening-night games

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to react to the NBA's opening day of games, including the Detroit Pistons rallying past the Boston Celtics, the Philadelphia 76ers ruining ring night for the New York Knicks and the Oklahoma City Thunder shutting down Victor Wembanyama in a big win against the San Antonio Spurs. They then welcome Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia to talk about his expectations this season as well as his thoughts on expansion and NBA Europe.
